description: SOC-thermal voltage model: V = OCV(SOC) - I*R(T), with Arrhenius resistance and capacity correction

cell.name: Generic solid-state Li cell (LiCoO2 / sulfide solid electrolyte / Li metal)
cell.source: Janek & Zeier (2016), Nat. Energy 1, 16141; QuantumScape & Solid Power patents

R_ref.note: Internal resistance at T_ref; SSE contributes higher interfacial resistance than liquid electrolyte

ocv_coefficients.description: OCV(SOC) = a0 + a1*SOC + a2*SOC^2 + a3*SOC^3 + a4*SOC^4 + a5*SOC^5
ocv_coefficients.source: Polynomial fit to representative solid-state Li cell discharge curve (similar to NMC with higher upper cut-off)

E_a.note: Activation energy for SSE ionic conductivity is higher than liquid electrolytes; sulfide SSE ~ 30-40 kJ/mol
E_a.source: Janek & Zeier (2016), Nat. Energy 1, 16141; Takada (2013), Acta Materialia 61, 759-770

alpha_c.note: Linear capacity temperature coefficient; similar to NMC-class cells
alpha_c.source: Schmalstieg et al. (2014), J. Power Sources 257, 325-334

dOCV_dT.note: Entropic coefficient; similar to NMC with LiCoO2 cathode
dOCV_dT.source: Thomas & Newman (2003), J. Electrochem. Soc. 150(2), A176-A192

temperature.note: 0 to 60 degC; SSE cells sometimes operated slightly warm to improve ionic conductivity
